# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH STAPHYLOCOCCUS LUGDUNENSIS

S. lugdunensis is the most pathogenic of the coagulase negative staphylococci with a severity of infection like that caused by S. aureus. Almost all isolates are methicillin-susceptible at the Minneapolis VAHCS.

Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) should be performed to rule out infectious endocarditis. Consult Cardiology or Infectious Diseases for more information.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.

[Approach to Endocarditis](endocarditis-approach-to)

Follow-up blood cultures should be obtained within 24-48 hours after initiating antimicrobial therapy to guide treatment.

# Duration of therapy:

The optimal duration of therapy has not been well established.  In patients with adequate source control and without complications, treatment for at least 2 weeks after last negative blood culture set is likely adequate. A longer duration may be required in complicated cases.

Therapy:
## Treatment for methicillin-susceptible S. lugdunensis (mecA negative)

Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h ($) R
< OR >
Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h ($$) R

## Treatment for methicillin-resistant S. lugdunensis (mecA positive)

Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) R
